answer: Yes, with limits. The `file` command (Operational mode) performs basic file and directory operations: `file [operation=]<value> [file-path=]<value> [new-file-path=]<value>`. Supported operations are rename (renames a file or directory), view (listing for a file or directory), delete (deletes a file), sha256sum and md5sum (hash checksums). `new-file-path` is only used with rename and follows pattern '[A-Za-z0-9 \-/\.]*'; `result` reports the file operation result. File system access is restricted to the current user's access, so not all files/directories are editable. Separately, `clear [-f] file [filetype=]<value> [target-file=]<value>` removes one particular file; filetype may be krp (only 1 krp may exist, so target-file is not needed), script (use `show script` to list available scripts) or swimage (deletes a downloaded swimage which was not yet installed). Examples: `file rename /tmp/a.log /tmp/b.log`, `file delete /tmp/a.log`, `clear file krp`.

Both are described as performing basic file and directory operations and both run in Operational mode, but `file` is the fuller command. `file-operation [[operation=]<value>] [new-file-path=]<value> [file-path=]<value>` supports only three operations: rename, delete, view, with parameters new-file-path (a new path to the file) and file-path (the path to the file), no defaults. `file [operation=]<value> [file-path=]<value> [new-file-path=]<value>` supports five operations: rename, delete, view, sha256sum (SHA256 hash checksum) and md5sum (md5 hash checksum), plus a `result` attribute for the file operation result, and its new-file-path is constrained to pattern '[A-Za-z0-9 \-/\.]*'. The `file` entity also carries the `clear file [filetype=]<value> [target-file=]<value>` form (filetypes krp, script, swimage) and `show file <filename>` to display file contents. So use `file` for checksums and for clearing files; `file-operation` covers only rename/delete/view.

Use `add file-server-<name> server-address <value> protocol <value> [server-port <value>] [user-name <value>] [password <value>] [initial-path <value>] [label <value>]`, with matching set/show/delete and `show file-servers`. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration. The protocol values are file, ftp, sftp, scp, http, https; ftp and http are applicable only when secure-mode is set to false, and `file` represents local storage including USB storage and requires initial-path to be provided. server-address may be an IPv4 address, IPv6 address or domain name. server-port is optional: if not provided the default for the selected protocol is used. Field limits: name String 0...64 characters, user-name 0..64, password 0...128, initial-path 0...256 (the directory used as source/destination), label 0...256. Example: `add file-server-139 server-address '10.220.227.139' protocol 'scp' user-name 'root' password 'Nokia' initial-path '/root'`.

Use `show filetype-<name> [last-completion-status] [last-transfer] [last-duration] [last-operation]`, available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. `name` is the file type for which the transfer happened. `last-completion-status` gives the last transfer status, `last-transfer` is the last transfer start timestamp as a date-time in the format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ (see the set-time command), `last-duration` is the last transfer duration as a time-interval, and `last-operation` reports the last transfer operation with values unknown, upload or download. For a per-operation breakdown with progress and byte counts, use `show transfer-status-<filetype>/<operation>` instead; note that transfer status only exists if at least one operation of that kind was done for the specified filetype.

Plain HTTP is supported but is off by default. Configure it with `set http-file-server [enabled <value>] [http-enabled <value>] [https-enabled <value>] [http-port <value>] [https-port <value>]`, and read it back with `show http-file-server [enabled] [http-enabled] [https-enabled] [http-port] [https-port] [url-base]`. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. `enabled` is the master switch for file server access, true/false, default true. `http-enabled` is true/false with default false; `https-enabled` is true/false with default true. `http-port` is a Number defaulting to 8980 and `https-port` defaults to 8981. `url-base` is show-only, the base URL used to redirect to the file transfer application, a String of 1..100 characters with default /transfer.

Use the `manifest` show commands (Operational and Candidate Configuration mode). `show manifest-<manifest-file> [manifest-signature] [downloaded-on] [information]` gives the file-level view: manifest-signature is a hex-string of length 0..1024, downloaded-on is the download timestamp in format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ, and information is a String 0..256. `show manifest-component-<manifest-file>/<equipment-type>/<name> [state] [version] [description]` gives per-package detail, where state is installed (software package installed), not-installed, installation-failed (install failed) or unknown, with default unknown; version is a string 0..64 and description 0..512. `show manifest-firmware-<manifest-file>/<equipment-type>/<fw-name> [fw-version]` lists the firmware included per equipment-type. Example: `show manifest-G30-R5.0.0-F-2021.11.04_20_04-46.manifest`.

No. Versions for the same firmware can be different per equipment-type within one software-load. Use `show packaged-fw-<location-id>/<swload-state>/<equipment-type>/<fw-name> [fw-version]`, or the shorter `show packaged-fw-<swload-state>/<equipment-type>/<fw-name> [fw-version]`; plain `show packaged-fw` lists all components' firmware versions in the load. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. `location-id` is <chassis-id>-<slot-id> of the SW load subcomponent, string 0..64 characters. `swload-state` is active (active software load), inactive or installable. `equipment-type` is the type of equipment (card, etc) that will use the firmware, String 0..32, and `fw-name` and `fw-version` are also String 0..32. Output looks like packaged-fw-active/CHM6/DCO-OEC-FPGA and packaged-fw-active/XMM4/FCP_FPGA.

Yes. `prepare-upgrade` has two options: validate, which validates the software label/manifest, and apply, which applies it. Syntax: `prepare-upgrade [-f] [-i] [-u] [option=]<value> [manifest=]<value> [[db-action=]<value>] [[clear-type=]<value>] [script=]<value> [new-admin-user=]<value> [new-admin-password=]<value>`, Operational mode. Flags: -h help, -i ignore validation failures, -u unattended (auto-activate software after prepare-upgrade apply), -f force without confirmation. `db-action` is empty-db, upgrade-db or rollback, default upgrade-db, and is valid for unattended upgrade only. `clear-type` is full (reset to factory defaults, the default), keep-networking (wipe but keep network configuration) or initialize-from-script, and is only valid for an unattended operation with db-action set to empty-db. new-admin-user (0..64 chars) and new-admin-password are mandatory for keep-networking or initialize-from-script. Example: `prepare-upgrade validate -f G40-R4.0.0-F-2021.06.03_08_22-sim-188.manifest`.

`clear [-f] recover-mode` clears the recover-mode flag. It clears the current recover-mode state of the NE, confirming the current configuration as is, re-enabling communication with the line cards and potentially reconfiguring the traffic settings. Because of that reconfiguration it may be traffic impacting. The command runs in Operational Mode and has no parameters; the only flag is -f, which forces the command without confirmation. Normal use is `clear recover-mode` (which prompts for confirmation) or `clear -f recover-mode` to skip the confirmation prompt.

Use `show software-load-<swload-state>` at NE level or `show software-load-<location-id>/<swload-state>` per card, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. `swload-state` is active (active software load), inactive, or installable. Selectable attributes are swload-version, swload-manifest, swload-prepared, swload-status, swload-information, swload-activation-type, swload-vendor, swload-product, swload-label, swload-delta-label and swload-pkg-type. swload-manifest and swload-prepared (true/false) are only of relevance for the installable load, as is swload-activation-type with values direct (no reboot type determined), warmstart (warm reboot required) and coldstart. swload-status covers status-unknown, validate/apply/activate/cancel in-progress, complete, failed and timeout variants. Examples: `show software-load-active`, `show software-load-1-5/active`. For a one-line summary use `swversion`.

Use `show software-location-<location-id>`, where location-id is the location of the equipment, a String of length 0..64 expressed as <chassis-id>-<slot-id>. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: `show software-location-1-5` retrieves software location information for the card in chassis 1, slot 5. To narrow to a particular load state on that slot, use `show software-load-<location-id>/<swload-state>`, for example `show software-load-1-5/active`, or go through the umbrella command: `show sw-management software-location-1-4 software-load-active`, which returns the sw-component list plus swload-version, swload-information, swload-vendor, swload-product, swload-label and swload-delta-label for that shelf-slot.

Use `show subtype-constraint-<card-type>/<subtype> [min-capacity] [max-capacity] [supported-applications] [unsupported-applications] [description]`, available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. card-type and subtype each represent a group of related PONs for a card type to which the constraints apply, strings of length 1...20. min-capacity is the minimum capacity supported by this subtype and max-capacity the maximum, both in gbps; a max-capacity of -1 means there is no maximum capacity constraint. supported-applications lists the applications supported by the subtype and unsupported-applications lists those not supported, both of application type; if either list is empty, then that constraint is not applicable. description is a string of length 1...255.

Use `show sw-component-<location-id>/<swload-state>/<name> [state] [version] [description]`, or `show sw-component-<swload-state>/<name>` for the NE-level view; plain `show sw-component` lists all SW load components and attributes. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. `state` is the package state and is what tells you about a failure: installed (software package installed), not-installed, installation-failed (software package install failed) or unknown, with default unknown. location-id is <chassis-id>-<slot-id>, string 0..64; swload-state is active, inactive or installable; name is the package name, String 0..256; version is 0..64 and description 0..512. Example: `show sw-component-1-5/active/frcu31_ztp_pkg`. To drill inside a failing package, use `show sw-subcomponent-<location-id>/<swload-state>/<sw-component-name>/<sw-subcomponent-name>`.

Use `show sw-container-<container-name> [equipment] [state] [description] [cpu-usage] [memory-usage] [uptime]`, which shows the list of OS-level containers; access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. `cpu-usage` is the current CPU usage by the container in percentage, Number range 0 ...100%, and in a multi-core system it indicates the overall usage relative to all cores. `memory-usage` is the current memory usage in percentage, range 0 ...100%. `state` is off (default state, not launched yet), up (container is up and running) or exited. `equipment` is a leafref to the card AID the container runs on, and `uptime` is the time since the container started. Examples: `show sw-container`, `show sw-container-frcu31-1-5_pyapi`. Per-service figures are available with `show sw-service-<sv-name>`, which also has cpu-usage and memory-usage.

Yes. `sw-control-rule` adds service-specific custom rules that override the default action upon service failure: `add sw-control-rule-<service-name> fail-action <value>`, `set sw-control-rule-<service-name> [fail-action <value>]`, `show sw-control-rule-<service-name> [fail-action]`, `delete sw-control-rule-<service-name>`. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. `service-name` is the name of the service to be monitored, String of length 0..64. `fail-action` takes three values: default-action, which performs the policy of restarting the service, then rebooting the system if the service is not recovered; ignore, which specifies that no automatic action is taken in case of service failure; and system-restart, which performs a warm restart of the system/card software immediately upon service failure. Example: `add sw-control-rule-xmm4-1-1_host_KeyManagement fail-action default-action`.

Yes, `show sw-management` shows information about software locations, activity and downloads. Syntax: `show sw-management [downloads|software-location-<shelf>-<slot> [software-load-active|software-load-inactive|software-load-installable] |software-load-active|software-load-inactive]`. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. `downloads` shows the download history (a list of downloaded manifest files). `software-load-active` shows active software and `software-load-inactive` shows inactive software, each returning the sw-component and packaged-fw entries plus swload-version, swload-information, swload-vendor, swload-product, swload-label and swload-delta-label. `software-location-<shelf>-<slot>` scopes the same view to one card, and accepts software-load-active, software-load-inactive or software-load-installable. Example: `show sw-management software-location-1-4 software-load-active`.

Use `show sw-service-<sv-name> [equipment] [location] [state] [state-details] [cpu-usage] [memory-usage] [uptime] [last-start-time] [reboot-count]`, or `show sw-services` for all services and containers on the node. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. `reboot-count` is the number of times a service has restarted, a uint16, and is the direct indicator of repeated restarts. Pair it with `last-start-time`, the time of the last service start/boot as a date-time in format YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ, and `uptime`, the time since the service turned up in days:hours:minutes. `state` is off (not being monitored), ok (ready and functional) or fail (failed to launch/turn-up or unresponsive), with `state-details` giving a brief description. `sv-name` is a unique Id per service instance containing card type, shelf and slot. Example: `show sw-service-frcu31-1-5_host_DpEncrMgr`.

`sw-subcomponent` adds one more level of key below the component, so you can see the individual packages inside a software load component. Syntax: `show sw-subcomponent-<location-id>/<swload-state>/<sw-component-name>/<sw-subcomponent-name> [state] [version] [description]`, or `show sw-subcomponent-<swload-state>/<sw-component-name>/<sw-subcomponent-name>` at NE level. `sw-component` is keyed only by <location-id>/<swload-state>/<name>. The reported attributes are the same in both: state with values installed, not-installed, installation-failed or unknown (default unknown), version (String 0..64) and description (String 0..512). sw-component-name and sw-subcomponent-name are strings of length 1..256. Both run in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: `show sw-subcomponent-1-5/active/frcu31_ztp_pkg/ztp.deb` versus `show sw-component-1-5/active/frcu31_ztp_pkg`.

Run `swversion`. It retrieves the active, inactive and/or installable versions of the software present on the network element. The command takes no parameters and is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Output lists the NE-level loads and then the same per slot, for example: software-load-active R4.0.0 G40-R4.0.0-F-2021.06.03_08_22-sim-188; software-load-inactive R4.0.0 G40-R4.0.0-F-2021.04.15_14_26-sim-112; software-load-installable R4.0.0 G40-R4.0.0-F-2021.06.03_08_22-sim-188; followed by software-load-1-1/active, software-load-1-1/inactive and software-load-1-1/installable rows. For more detail on any one of them use `show software-load-<swload-state>` or `show sw-management software-load-active`.

Use `show third-party-fw-<fw-name> [file-status] [path] [version] [crc] [vendor] [part-number] [nsa-upgrade-version] [present-in-eqpt] [applicable-eqpt]`, in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. `file-status` is the firmware file status with values valid, invalid or missing. `crc` is the cyclic redundancy check of the firmware image, used to validate the file when present, string 0...64. `path` is the path for the firmware image, string 0...255. `applicable-eqpt` is the list of resources that this firmware can be applied to, and `present-in-eqpt` is the list of resources that already contain this version; both lists have max-elements 80. `nsa-upgrade-version` gives the versions from where the upgrade is non service affecting (nsa), string 0...255. vendor and part-number are strings 0...64.

Set it on the `transfer` entity: `set transfer [http-proxy <value>]`, read it back with `show transfer [debug-log-optional-content] [http-proxy]`. Access mode is Operational and Candidate configuration mode. `http-proxy` is the proxy server for internally-generated HTTP requests leaving the NE, which includes certificate revocation-related requests, that is CRL downloads and OCSP requests. Note that this proxy is not used for file transfers. The value is a string of length 0..1024 in the format '[http://]<host>[:<port>]', where 'http://' is optional, <host> may be the IPv4 address, IPv6 address or DNS name of the proxy server, and <port> is optional; if <port> is omitted the default is 1080. Example: `set transfer http-proxy http://1.2.3.4:1080`.

Use `show transfer-status-<filetype>/<operation> [last-completion-status] [last-transfer] [last-duration] [transfer-type] [session-id] [session-user-name] [filename] [transfer-progress] [bytes-transferred] [total-bytes] [details]`, in Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode. `operation` is upload or download. `transfer-progress` is the transfer completion percentage, 0-100 percent, default 0; `bytes-transferred` and `total-bytes` are uint64 byte counts defaulting to 0, and total-bytes stays zero until known at the transfer start. `details` gives the transfer phase: completed, Failed, idle, preparation or transfer, default idle. `last-completion-status` is a String 0..128 such as success, fail, in-progress or unknown; unknown occurs when the system reboots while a transfer is in-progress. `transfer-type` is sync or async. In synchronous mode a textual progress bar is rendered live in the CLI; for asynchronous transfers (-a) use this command.

Use `show upgrade-status-<resource> [to-swload-version] [status] [start-time] [end-time] [step] [step-start-time] [details]`, in Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode. Status is reported at NE level, chassis level and card level; `resource` (string 0..255) specifies the object, and for ne and chassis the results provide aggregated summaries of all cards in that scope, so start at the ne resource and then drill into chassis and card to locate the failure. `status` values include idle, upgrade-in-progress, upgrade-complete, upgrade-partially-failed, upgrade-failed, validate-in-progress/-failed/-complete, apply-in-progress/-failed/-complete, activate-in-progress/-failed/-complete, cancel-in-progress/-complete/-failed and no-communication; the default is idle. `step` is the identifier for the current upgrade step (string 0..128) and `step-start-time` when it was initiated; start-time and end-time show 'na' if idle or unfinished since startup, and `details` (0..255) carries the detail.

Use `upload [-a] [-s] filetype=debug-log (destination=<url> | file-server=<name> [path=<path>]) debug-entity=<value> [optional-content=<value>[,<value>]*]`, Operational mode. debug-log uploads logs for diagnostic troubleshooting and includes all other logs; debug-entity is mandatory and targets a chassis or card (if absent, all data is included). -a runs it asynchronously (check with `show transfer-status`); in synchronous mode a live progress bar is rendered. -s skips secure verification (TLS for HTTPS, ssh known host for SCP/SFTP). Certificates differ: filetypes local-certificate, peer-certificate and trusted-certificate require `certificate-name` to name the specific certificate, except for trusted-certificate where omitting the name exports all trusted certificates as a bundle. Only the public part is exported, private keys are not exported, and the output files are in P7 pem format. Example: `upload trusted-certificate destination=sftp://jz@100.113.83.14:/home/jz/demos/all.pem`.

Use `show ztp [ztp-mode] [ztp-state] [ztp-details] [ztp-completion-status]`, in Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode. `ztp-state` is the current state of the ZTP service and walks through ztp-init (the default), dhcp-in-progress, image-download-in-progress, image-install-in-progress, custom-script-execution-in-progress, multi-chassis-setup-in-progress, configuration-apply-in-progress, ztp-completed, ztp-state-unknown, ztp-disabled and wait-before-ztp-restart. `ztp-completion-status` summarizes completion on the node as not-completed (default) or completed. `ztp-details` is additional information on the current state, String 0..256. `ztp-mode` is the user-set mode, disabled or enabled with default enabled; it is set via the change-ztp-mode RPC, which is allowed even when the NBI is locked.
